evals.prompt: Summarise docs/meetings/raw/2026-11-17.md. The transcript is from Monday's product sync with the Fernhill Studio team.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the transcript, works out who is who from speaker labels and greetings, reads the 2 to 3 newest summaries in docs/meetings/summarized/ to match headings and density, and saves docs/meetings/summarized/2026-11-17.md with an H1 'Meeting Summary: [Topic], [subtitle]', a Date and Participants line, and only the sections that have real content (Decisions nearly always). Bullets stand alone, name who decided or raised what, and use absolute dates.
assertions: The summary is saved as docs/meetings/summarized/2026-11-17.md, the same file name as the transcript
The newest existing summaries are read before the new one is drafted
Relative dates spoken in the meeting (such as 'next Monday') appear as absolute dates in the summary
The participant list includes people identified in the transcript body, not only the name on the metadata line

evals.prompt: what did we decide about the pricing page launch date?
evals.expected_output: The agent lists the summaries, reads their H1s, reads every match on the topic (not only recent ones), and answers from summaries first in a few sentences or bullets in date order, latest decision last, calling out any reversal and stating the current position. Every claim carries a dated citation such as (2026-05-18 summary). If nothing matches, it says 'No meeting covers this' and names the closest topic.
assertions: Every factual claim in the answer carries a citation with a YYYY-MM-DD date and its source (summary or transcript)
When more than one meeting covers the topic, the answer runs in date order with the latest decision last and states the current position
No decision is stated that the cited meetings do not support
